name: Caroline Polachek
label: Perpetual Novice
lede: A haunted-house idea in Boulder turned into a band, a Beyoncé credit and an iPod ad, and then Caroline Polachek made the album Pitchfork ranked No. 2 of 2023.

eras.title: From Tokyo to a Boulder dorm
eras.text: Caroline Polachek grows up between Tokyo and Greenwich, then starts a band in a Colorado college town with a plan to score haunted houses. Two moves and one new member later, Chairlift is a Williamsburg band with a record deal.

years.h: Caroline Polachek is born in Manhattan
years.p: Tokyo takes her from age one to six; Greenwich, Connecticut, takes over after.
years.xp: Wikipedia gives her father as a Chinese history scholar of Ashkenazi Jewish descent and her mother as of Scottish and English heritage.

years.h: Two Colorado students plan music for haunted houses
years.p: Caroline Polachek and Aaron Pfenning meet at the University of Colorado Boulder in October 2005. The haunted houses never happen. Chairlift does.

years.h: Chairlift leave Los Angeles for Williamsburg
years.p: The Daylight Savings EP starts in April at New Monkey Studio with bassist Kyle McCabe. By August the band is living in Brooklyn.

years.h: [[Patrick Wimberly|5708b562-3880-4be8-9dab-f2bb2834fbf8]] completes the trio and Kanine signs it
years.p: He joins early in 2007; the Kanine Records deal comes that June.
years.xp: Wimberly would outlast one founder and become the other half of Chairlift's second act. He went on to produce for Beyoncé, Solange, MGMT and Blood Orange, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: An iPod ad does the marketing
eras.text: The debut goes out on a small label, one song lands in an Apple commercial, and Columbia reissues the record. Then one founder leaves for a solo project and Chairlift becomes a duo.

years.h: Does You Inspire You arrives on Kanine
years.p: Britt Myers produces the first Chairlift album. Pitchfork gives it 5.6; Metacritic lands on 68.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Pitchfork scored it 5.6/10 and Prefix 7.5/10, and NME singled out its 80s arrangements of flutes and chiming guitars. Robert Christgau marked a choice cut.

years.cap: Caroline Polachek at South by Southwest, Austin
years.src: Wikipedia: Does You Inspire You · Wikipedia: Caroline Polachek
years.h: "Bruises" turns up in an iPod nano ad
years.p: Yahoo! News reported on September 16, 2008 that the commercial gave Chairlift a boost.
years.xp: The song became the thing Chairlift were introduced as for years. Wikipedia cites Yahoo! News's headline: "Chairlift Gets A Boost From iPod Nano Ad."

years.cap: Chairlift in the studio at The Current, St. Paul, April 2009
years.h: Columbia picks up Does You Inspire You and adds two songs
years.p: "Le Flying Saucer Hat" and "Dixie Gypsy" are new, with an extended "Make Your Mind Up". The "Evident Utensil" video is up for a VMA in Breakthrough Video.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the album had sold 11,000 copies in the United States as of April 2009, a small number set against how many people had heard "Bruises" in an ad. The MTV nomination for "Evident Utensil" was at the 2009 Video Music Awards.

years.h: Aaron Pfenning leaves to make records as Rewards
years.p: Chairlift becomes a duo: Caroline Polachek and Patrick Wimberly.

eras.title: Something, and a Beyoncé credit
eras.text: The duo makes the record critics rank. Then Polachek and Wimberly help write a track on a Beyoncé album.

years.h: "Amanaemonesia" goes out first
years.p: "Sidewalk Safari" follows in October and "Met Before" in November, three singles before Something arrives.

years.cap: Caroline Polachek at World Cafe Live, Philadelphia, January 2012
years.h: Something is the record critics rank
years.p: Dan Carey and Alan Moulder produce. Pitchfork gives it 8, Metacritic 76, and it debuts at No. 184 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: The album came out in the US on Columbia on January 24, 2012, with a UK release through Young Turks a day earlier. Polachek named Strawberry Switchblade, Bill Nelson, Yellow Magic Orchestra, OMD and Art of Noise as influences, alongside black metal and Japanese classical music. Stereogum ranked it ninth on its 50 best albums of 2012.

years.h: A music video you steer yourself
years.p: For "Met Before", Jordan Fish directs a choose-your-own-adventure. BuzzFeed ranked it among the year's best videos.

years.src: Crack Magazine: · Wikipedia: Caroline Polachek · Wikipedia: Patrick Wimberly
years.h: Beyoncé records a song Caroline Polachek co-wrote
years.p: Polachek is co-writer and co-producer of "No Angel" on Beyoncé, with Patrick Wimberly co-producing. Crack says the credit brought a Grammy nomination.
years.xp: Crack ties her Grammy nomination to the song. ABC News dates the nomination differently (2012), so check before repeating it.

eras.title: A laptop in Rome, then Moth
eras.text: Polachek makes a solo record under a pseudonym, and Chairlift makes a third and last album.

years.h: A solo album on a laptop, as Ramona Lisa
years.p: She writes Arcadia at a Villa Medici residency in Rome and calls it pastoral electronic music.
years.xp: Wikipedia says she made the whole album on her laptop, recording vocals into its built-in microphone in hotel closets, airport gates and dressing rooms while touring with Chairlift. Pitchfork gave it 6.8; Under the Radar put it at No. 83 for the year and Dazed Digital at No. 18.

years.cap: Caroline Polachek of Chairlift at Treefort Music Fest, Boise, 2016
years.h: Moth is the third Chairlift album, and the last
years.p: Wimberly and Polachek write and produce it with Robin Hannibal and Cecil Frena at their Brooklyn studio.
years.xp: "Ch-Ching" came out October 14, 2015, then "Romeo", "Crying In Public" and "Moth To The Flame". Metacritic's score is 73; the album peaked at No. 7 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart. Rolling Stone called it "a record where love, music and love for music come together beautifully."

years.h: Chairlift announce they're done
years.p: A final tour follows in spring 2017.

eras.title: Under her own name
eras.text: A last tour, a second pseudonym and a feature on Charli XCX's mixtape come first. Then a record that says Caroline Polachek on the cover.

years.src: Wikipedia: Caroline Polachek discography · Wikipedia: Arcadia (Ramona Lisa album)
years.h: A second pseudonym, CEP, and a short record
years.p: Drawing the Target Around the Arrow comes out on Pannonica, the Bella Union imprint that also put out Arcadia in Europe.

years.h: She guests on Charli XCX's Pop 2
years.p: Wikipedia notes she later appears on Charli's Crash (2022) too.

years.cap: Caroline Polachek in The Current's studio, St. Paul, December 2019
yt: "So Hot You're Hurting My Feelings" (lyric video)
years.h: Pang is her first album under her own name
years.p: It comes out on her own Perpetual Novice imprint with The Orchard. Pitchfork gives it 7.3, Metacritic 82, and Dazed puts it No. 1 on its albums of 2019.
years.xp: Producers included Danny L Harle, Dan Carey, A. G. Cook, Jim-E Stack, Daniel Nigro and Andrew Wyatt. "Door" came first, on June 19, 2019, and "So Hot You're Hurting My Feelings" on September 16. Wikipedia reports that the latter reached RIAA Gold in 2024.
play: So Hot You're Hurting My Feelings

eras.title: Lockdown, Spain and a run of singles
eras.text: Her father dies, she moves to Spain with her main collaborator, and two years of singles build the next album in public.

years.h: Her father dies of COVID-19
years.p: Wikipedia and Crack both note it. She later relocates to Spain with Danny L Harle because of visa issues.
years.xp: Crack reports the visa issues and the move, and that she drew on flamenco and worked with Arca ("My favourite DJ in the world", she says). The record that came out of it was not built as a mourning album.

years.src: NPR: · Wikipedia: Desire, I Want to Turn Into You
years.h: "Bunny Is a Rider" opens the Desire run
years.p: NPR notes it gained traction on social media.
years.xp: The song starts a single run that includes "Billions", "Sunset", "Welcome to My Island" and "Blood and Butter". A behind-the-scenes clip from the video shoot is on YouTube.

years.h: "Billions" is Pitchfork's Best New Track
years.p: She and Harle wrote and produced it. Rolling Stone called it a trip-hop inspired, hallucinogenic epic.
years.xp: The Fader said it turned Pure Moods-era new age into something utterly splendid. It hit No. 4 on Gorilla vs. Bear's 2022 list and No. 14 on Slant's. The B-side reworked "Long Road Home", her collaboration with Oneohtrix Point Never.

years.cap: Caroline Polachek opening for Dua Lipa, First Avenue, Minneapolis, March 2022
yt: "So Hot You're Hurting My Feelings", Glastonbury 2022
years.h: She supports Dua Lipa and Megan Thee Stallion
years.p: ABC News says she toured with both. A video of "So Hot" from Glastonbury 2022 is below.

eras.title: Desire
eras.text: The album lands at No. 2 on Pitchfork's list, and the tour that follows has a volcano on stage.

years.cap: Desire, I Want to Turn Into You (2023)
q: She's an artist at the peak of her powers.
years.src: Wikipedia: Desire, I Want to Turn Into You · ABC News:
years.h: Desire, I Want to Turn Into You lands on Valentine's Day
years.p: Pitchfork gives it 8.7 and Best New Music, then ranks it No. 2 of 2023. Metacritic lands on 94.
years.xp:
Perpetual Novice, The Orchard and Sony released it. Wikipedia lists Danny L Harle, Dan Nigro, Jim-E Stack, Sega Bodega and Ariel Rechtshaid as producers, Grimes and Dido on "Fly to You", and Oneohtrix Point Never on "Long Road Home". It is her first album to chart across several territories: UK No. 23, US Billboard 200 No. 87.

The New York Times also put it at No. 2; DIY and Exclaim! named it No. 1. The 66th Grammys nominated it for Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical. Scores from Wikipedia's reception box.
play: Desire, I Want to Turn Into You

years.big: Ferocious, unhinged, comedic, sexy and an absolute mess
q: I'm a deep believer in what lies behind the story.
years.h: Pedro Almodóvar is on the mood board
years.p: Polachek's own words for the women in Almodóvar's films, a frame she took into Desire.
years.xp: Crack reports that the album grew from a song written during the Pang sessions in 2018 that didn't fit. Polachek says Harle didn't executive produce it because she had already begun writing, and adds: "We have so much faith in each other."

years.cap: Caroline Polachek at The Warfield, San Francisco, 2023
years.h: The Spiraling Tour builds a volcano and plays 70 shows
years.p: From Brighton on February 10 to Brisbane on December 13, with Radio City Music Hall on May 20.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Doss, Ethel Cain, Sudan Archives, George Clanton, Toro y Moi, Alex G and Magdalena Bay among the support acts, and the Sydney Opera House on December 4. Stage: a large volcano, smoke billowing from the top, and a cracked clock counting down a minute.

years.src: Wikipedia: Desire, I Want to Turn Into You
years.h: Desire gets four more songs
years.p: The Everasking Edition includes Weyes Blood on "Butterfly Net".
